## Summary

**Deliverable:** `evaluation/af-rotor-abstracts-critique.md` (created — supersedes Mission Control's "deliverable not produced" note; the file now exists with all required sections).

**Recommendation: Major Revision.** The abstracts are well-structured, honestly label hypothesis-generating content, and use correct EP formalism ($\lambda = \text{CV}\times\text{ERP}$, monodomain, Pennes bioheat). But four fixable Major issues stand out.

**Citation verification vs cardiology-canon-v2:**
- ✅ **Verified exact:** ESC AF ref 711 (Katritsis, *JACC* 2013;62:2318–2325); refs 952–953 (Thanigaimani; Kumagai).
- ✅ **Content genuine:** 2017 SCD Guideline §3.4 really does contain the "spiral wave reentry … rotor … curved wavefront and wavetail pivoting around an excitable but unexcited core" text (general functional-reentry models).
- ❌ **MAJOR misattribution:** ESC AF **ref 709 is Mohanty et al.** (Natale group), *Heart Rhythm* 2016;13:830–835 — **not Narayan**. Title/journal/pages correct, first author wrong. Repeated in Abstracts 3 and 5.
- ❌ **MAJOR misapplied source:** 2018 Bradycardia Guideline (S5.1-1/-8) used for atrial Cx43/fibrosis claims (Abstracts 1, 4); scope mismatch. On-point canon sources exist (2018 CSANZ AF; ESC AF 952–953).

**Other Majors:** Abstract 1 overstates rotor certainty (source explicitly calls it "debated"); Abstract 5 conflates the *electrical* "excitable-but-unexcited core" with *perfusion/thermal* properties, and contradicts Abstract 4's rotor-drift thesis.

**Per-item scores** (Mech | Evidence | Rigor | Clinical | Precision): A1 4/3/4/4/3 · A2 4/3/4/4/4 · A3 4/3/4/5/4 (strongest) · A4 4/2/4/4/3 · A5 2/2/3/3/3 (weakest).

**Next actions:** Authors should (1) fix the ref-709 author, (2) re-ground connexin/fibrosis claims to CSANZ/ESC AF, (3) soften Abstract 1's framing, (4) repair Abstract 5's premise and reconcile with Abstract 4. No fabricated citations were introduced by this review.Stop reason: end_turn
